question: Does moving the ordinary BTC completed-4h-close <= EMA20 veto before its original six-day reservation restore later eligible entries, while retaining the case-first BTC clock and the independent original ALT 24h-spacing sleeve?
single_variable: Only move the ordinary BTC EMA20 veto from after the original six-day frequency reservation to immediately before it. Keep the causal breadth rule, case branch priority and half-target/half-six-day exit, ordinary BTC 144h VectorBT exit, BTC six-day reservation, ALT fixed 6h exit and 24h admission spacing, 50/50 starting capital, no transfers, and fees unchanged.
baseline: Existing case-first dual BTC schedule, then suppress ordinary events above the completed 4h EMA20; suppressed events keep the earlier reservation occupied.
candidate: Apply the same ordinary BTC EMA20 gate before the original per-epoch six-day-plus-24h-minimum frequency admission, then preserve the case-first six-day dual-source schedule.
alt: Reuse original freq36_ALT fixed 6h exit stream and 24h minimum admission spacing unchanged.
fees: Existing VectorBT 0.05% taker on ordinary BTC entry and exit; native policy 4 BTC case fills with the original maker/taker exit legs. Historical account return is fee-only. 2026 account marks apply locally archived realized Binance USD-M funding.
capital: Independent BTC and ALT sleeves, 50% initial capital each, no transfers or rebalancing; each sleeve deploys its own capital as in the frozen extension risk study.
controls: Reuse a matched random control only when both asset and exact event clock match the existing strategy. Newly admitted clocks receive no imputed control; no new controls are fitted in this experiment.
known_trade_audit: Explicitly audit the 2026-09-15 19:20 UTC BTC 5% case target and any six-day booking that prevents it.
